answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with a bonded-entry rule: every identity must lock a copper-weight deposit of real value before transacting. New identities cannot trade at dawn on day one; they must collect signed vouchers from established agents, each risking part of their own bond by vouching. A cipher-signed audit trail links every vouchee to its sponsors, so one detected fraud burns the deposit and taints the whole chain. Attackers pay thousands of deposits plus the reputational price of recruiting honest sponsors, while honest newcomers earn entry cheaply.
